$comment: The Explore canon. Every preset is also a worked example of the Build grammar, so each must be expressible as {dataset, measure, dimension, period, filters}. If a preset cannot be expressed in the builder vocabulary, either extend the vocabulary or drop the preset. A chart whose dataset has a definition in dimensions.json renders that definition.
evergreen_test: Would this chart still be worth showing in 2035? If the title names a specific scheme, brand or year, it fails and belongs in the events layer instead.

$status.$comment: Every preset carries a status, so the gap between the canon and what the cube can serve is visible rather than discovered chart by chart. The UI renders anything not live as a 'coming when X lands' entry, and cross-checks the authored status against what the cube actually resolves: a disagreement is shown as a warning, because a stale status is worse than none.
$status.live: Renders from the cube as built.
$status.blocked: Correctly specified. Waiting on a deliverable named in requires.
$status.invalid: The preset's own configuration is wrong. requires names the fix.
$status.precedence: status is the worst outstanding state; requires lists every outstanding item, not just the worst.
$status.on_unblocking: When a dataset a preset waits on lands, re-run the triage before building the chart. The canon was written well ahead of the data, so some blocked presets will want rewriting rather than unblocking.

$note_templates.$comment: A note that states a figure must be templated from the build, or it drifts the moment the data moves. note_template resolves {dotted.path} against the manifest, the preset's dataset entry in it, and the preset's measure and dimension definitions; |pct formats a proportion. A plain note may not contain a figure at all: the UI flags one that does.

$composite.$comment: A deliberate, closed exception to one-chart-one-question, for the two questions that only exist as a comparison of two series. Not a sixth shape: both render through the trend renderer. Composite presets are never offered in the builder, and the UI flags them as a curated comparison so a reader does not mistake them for something the grammar can express.

defaults.$year_change_measure_comment: The measure whose floor (guards.min_denominator in config/measures.json) decides when a change on a year ago is withheld.

phrases.$comment: The words around a figure's change on a year ago, a ranking's window and a month the address names that the chart cannot show. Each is a template: the placeholders it may use are listed in config/narrative/rules.json, and pipeline/tests/test_site_config.py holds every template to them and to the banned words. A template says what the data shows, never why. {change|pct} is a proportion shown by one rule: under 10% with one decimal, otherwise whole.

defaults.$comment: Chart-level defaults that are not per-preset decisions. mix_smoothing: monthly share on survivors data swings too hard to read, so a mix chart defaults to a trailing share and offers monthly as a toggle. top_n_basis: which window ranks the values that keep their own line; the rest become one remainder series.

matrix.$comment: The grid of two fields crossed (D-114). rows and columns: how many lines of the largest values a side shows when the visitor has picked none; the rest stand together in one line. step_fractions: the upper end of each shade step as a fraction of the largest figure in the grid (the last is 1); the colours are the --scale-N tokens in src/styles/site.css, one for each step. cells: what a cell holds when the question does not say (a count shows vehicles, a share shows a share of all).

defaults.$colour_slots_comment: The line palette has eight colours (src/lib/theme.ts: no set of colours keeps more lines apart under colour blindness). On a mix chart the first colour_slots_by_trailing go to the largest series over the trailing window, the rest by peak rolling share over the preset's period, and any series beyond the palette is drawn as a grey context line. 5 keeps every current contender on the owner_country chart in colour while leaving three slots for the categories that carried earlier decades.

mix_default_start.$comment: A mix chart over all time crushes its story into the right of the frame whenever the dimension spent decades with one category. The default start is the first month the dimension had something to show: at least min_categories categories above min_share, sustained for sustain_months, measured on the 12-month rolling mix so it does not move with monthly noise. All time stays available as a toggle and is never the default. Computed in the browser, like the rolling share and the suppression guards, so these numbers change without a rebuild.
mix_default_start.$threshold_note: min_share 0.005 puts powertrain at 2009-10, where hybrids first became visible; 0.02 puts it at 2018-07 and hides the nine-year ramp. Do not lower it below 0.004: at 0.003 powertrain falls back to 1938-01, because 1940s diesel sat near 0.36% and the now-extinct Other category near 0.71%. The qualifying run is 202 months and the nearest non-qualifying run is 5, so sustain_months is what rejects the mid-century near-misses.
mix_default_start.$cardinality_note: Only low-cardinality dimensions. The test measures diversity, and diversity saturates immediately when a dimension has hundreds of values: on make it returns whatever month the denominator floor allows and the composition clause never binds.

builder.$comment: The Build page: a question a visitor builds (what to measure, what to compare, which vehicles to keep, D-058), drawn through the same panel and resolver as Explore. Values and filters are summed from the fact table; without them a chart reads the slices. A measure offers only the dimensions it lists here (each with the words the sentence uses for it), and of those only the ones that resolve and draw against the cube as built. Ids name what config/measures.json and config/dimensions.json define; the words are for visitors. not_offered tells the visitor what is missing and why (D-044).

notices.$comment: What the page says when a link asks for something the page cannot give and shows the nearest question instead. The address is corrected as it is for a condition the page cannot apply; the words say so, so a link never quietly counts something else. Placeholders: config/narrative/rules.json.
notices.dataset: This link asked to count {asked}, which this build does not have. It is counting {shown} instead.
notices.by: This link asked to break the figures down by {asked}, which is not available for {dataset}. It shows {shown} instead.
notices.left_out: This link named “{asked}” for {field}, which is not a value that can be chosen here, so it was left out.
notices.by2: This link asked for a second breakdown by {asked}, which this question cannot have. It shows the question without one.
notices.value2: This link named values for a second breakdown, but it names no second breakdown, so the values were left out.
notices.snapshot: This link named the snapshot “{asked}”, which is not a month, so it was left out.
notices.pin_same: Pinned to {pinned|month}, the snapshot month this page shows.
notices.pin_newer: Pinned to {pinned|month}: the window keeps ending in that month. The figures come from the newer snapshot of {date|date}, so they may differ from those seen when it was pinned.
notices.pin_newer_plain: Pinned to {pinned|month}. The figures come from the newer snapshot of {date|date}, so they may differ from those seen when it was pinned.
notices.pin_newer_open: Pinned to {pinned|month}. This chart always runs to the newest month, {latest|month}, so it shows the newer snapshot of {date|date}, and its figures may differ from those seen when it was pinned.
notices.pin_uncovered: Pinned to {pinned|month}, which this chart has no figures for, so it shows the newest month, {latest|month}, of the snapshot of {date|date}.
notices.pin_ahead: This link is pinned to {pinned|month}, a snapshot this site does not have yet. It shows the snapshot of {date|date}.
notices.pin_kept: Pinned to {pinned|month}. These are the figures of the snapshot of {date|date}, kept on this site.
notices.pin_kept_missing: The snapshot of {date|date} that this link is pinned to cannot answer this question.
notices.pin_kept_withheld: The snapshot of {date|date} that this link is pinned to does not say that small counts were hidden in the fields this question names, so its figures for this question are not shown.
notices.small_cells_hidden: This table has small counts hidden, and this site does not draw a table like that yet.

builder.$datasets_comment: What a question counts. The first is the default, and an address with no build.dataset means it. Each is offered only where the build made it, and only the dimensions, values and conditions that dataset carries are offered with it. A text that differs by dataset (note, dimension_notes) is an object keyed by dataset id.
builder.$cannot_cross_comment: Pairs of fields where each value of one sits under a single value of the other (a model under its brand, a brand under its group), so a grid of the two would be empty except along one line and its empty cells would be empty by construction, not by what people bought. Measured on the 2026-10 fact tables of both datasets: each value of the first sat under one value of the second, except that two models of the survivors and one of true registrations sat under two brands (and so two groups and countries). The data map's rolls_up_to gives make to parent_group and owner_country and model to make. Build offers no second breakdown that makes one of these pairs. Also measured: segment_group (vehicle class) sits under one vehicle_type (registered as), but vehicle_type is a condition only and never a breakdown, so no pair is listed for it; add [segment_group, vehicle_type] if it is ever offered. On the 2026-10 fact table of true registrations on the wider scope each of its five registered-as types sits under exactly one passenger-or-commercial group (Passenger holds one, Commercial four), so [trade_group, vehicle_type] is listed; vehicle_type is still a condition only, and the pair is listed so that offering it as a breakdown later cannot make a grid empty by construction. segment (vehicle type in Build's words) and segment_group are not nested (4 of 6 segments have more than one class), and are crossed. Build also reads the data map itself (src/lib/nesting.ts): a field that rolls up to another there, through any number of steps, is not crossed with it, nor with a dimension read from that field alone, so NZTA's class code is not crossed with the registered-as type or its passenger-or-commercial reading (D-122). This list stays for pairs the map does not record.
builder.$period_when_comparing_comment: A question that names values (brands, models) opens on the last ten years: most named values have little or no history before that, and all time would spend most of the chart on empty decades. The time row still offers all time.
builder.$period_by_shape_comment: A distribution sums its whole period, so all time would mix decades whose records differ (docs/MODEL_AND_AGE.md, before 2007). A map opens on the last 12 months, the vehicles whose owners' addresses are most recent. A ranking of the values a visitor chose opens on the last 12 months, the window the ranking of every value opens on (D-111). The time row still offers all time, except where a chart pins its shape and the period would not fit it.
builder.$ranking_period_comment: The time row offers this period too wherever it makes the chart a league (a high-cardinality breakdown such as brand), so a visitor can rank the latest 12 months and switch back to the lines. Manufacturer group is high cardinality in config/dimensions.json, as brand is, so a 12-month window ranks it too (D-050).

measures.$top_n_comment: The values that keep their own line on a mix chart; the rest become one remainder, All other. Reserved tokens (not recorded, no reference match) keep their own grey line and never join it (D-046). make and parent_group as brand-share uses. built_in is capped at 10 of its 46 values in the 2026-09 cube: its country is not recorded for almost every vehicle first registered before about 1986, and that gap shows as its own Not recorded line.

note.registrations_surviving: Share, not volume. These are vehicles still registered at the snapshot, so older months are thinned by scrappage and a count would partly measure it. Share removes the shrinkage every group shares, but groups leave the register at different rates, so older months lean towards groups whose vehicles stay registered longer.

measures.$dimensions_comment: A count by a breakdown draws one line per chosen value, so it needs the fact table; with no breakdown it is the total of the vehicles kept.

note.registrations_surviving: Vehicles still registered today, not sales. Older months are thinned by scrappage, so a line that falls back in time partly measures how many have left the register since, and groups leave it at different rates.

measures.phrase: the share and number of vehicles
measures.$parts_comment: Two charts, one above the other, never one chart with two axes: the share, then the count, of the same question. Offers the dimensions both parts offer.

measures.note_template: The combined share of the {measure.top_n} largest in each month. Membership is recomputed monthly, so the line reflects concentration rather than the fortunes of a fixed set. A falling line means the largest hold less of the market: more may be competing, or the same ones may be sharing it more evenly. Vehicles with no match in the brand list count in the total but never take a place, which holds the line down in the early decades.

dimension_notes.$comment: What a canon preset says about a dimension in its own note, which a built chart would otherwise lose. Here rather than in a dimension's public_note so Explore does not show it twice.
dimension_notes.segment: The register records most SUVs as station wagons, so they count as cars here.

import_status.registrations_surviving: These are vehicles still registered at the snapshot, and new and used vehicles leave the register at different rates, so an older month's split may differ from what was bought at the time. In recent cohorts used imports leave faster, which understates their share; in some older cohorts it runs the other way.

dimension_notes.owner_country: Ownership is as at today, not at registration: every year shown counts each brand under the country that owns it now.
dimension_notes.parent_group: Group ownership is as at today, not at registration: every year shown counts each brand under the group that owns it now.
dimension_notes.region: Where each vehicle's registered owner lives now, from their most recent address: not where the vehicle is driven, and not necessarily where it was first registered. Rental and lease fleets count at the address of the company that owns them. Each owner is placed in a region by their district, and a few districts cross a regional boundary, so their vehicles are counted in one region even where part of the district lies in another.

not_offered: Two breakdowns drawn over time, as a line for each combination. A crossing is drawn for one window, the last 12 months or one month; move the window to see it change.

not_offered.text: Every vehicle registered each month, including those since removed from the register. This build does not carry true registrations, so these figures count vehicles still registered today.

not_offered: Registrations before the first month of the dashboard's data, by brand or model. Stats NZ's long-run series has totals and a split into new and ex-overseas, no brand or model; the Explore page draws it where this build carries it.

presets.note: Ownership is as at today, not at registration. A Fuso registered while Daimler Truck controlled it counts as Japanese-owned, because ARCHION owns Fuso now. This chart answers who owns these brands now.

presets.question: How has each powertrain's share of registrations changed?
New or second-hand? The balance over time.
presets.note: These are vehicles still registered at the snapshot, and new and used vehicles leave the register at different rates, so an older month's split may differ from what was bought at the time. A rising remainder here is the market fragmenting across groups too small to rank; the concentration chart measures that directly rather than leaving it to be inferred.

presets.question: Is the market getting more crowded?
presets.note_template: The combined share of the {measure.top_n} largest brands in each month. Membership is recomputed monthly, so the line reflects concentration rather than the fortunes of a fixed set of brands. A falling line means the largest brands hold less of the market: more brands may be competing, or the same brands may be sharing it more evenly. In the early decades, makes with no match in the brand list count in the total but never take a place, which holds the line down.
